text:
Anya L: Heads up — saw a p99 increase (~+210ms) on tiny-seq traffic right after the 10:30 canary. Looks correlated with batcher config change that landed earlier today. anyone oncall?
Kevin M: that was my canary — I bumped batcher.min_batch_fill from 0.05 -> 0.18 to try and improve throughput for medium sequences. Canary at 10%. didn't catch p99 locally. :confused: 
deploy-bot: canary rollout started by Kevin M at 1917654000 (10%).
Anya L: attaching quick perf link: https://observability/redwood/rt/p99?range=1h (note tiny-seq baseline was ~80ms, spiked to 290ms at 10:32)
observability-bot: KV cache hit ratio: stable at 0.74 -> 0.71; requests/sec steady. Microbatch wait time avg: +35ms, std dev up. CPU spinups increased on canary hosts.
Sasha P: I pulled an async profile from one of the canary nodes — scheduler queues show more frequent microbatch coalescing delays. The kernel-autoselect switched from "legacy-fp16" -> "aligned-fused" for small sequence lengths due to the changed batch distribution. The fused kernel has better throughput at scale but ~150ms/setup overhead on first run for small batches.
Sasha P: profiler snippet:
```
# perf-summary
service: runtime-canary-1
hotspot: kernel_init (150ms)
queue: wait-for-batch (avg 28ms)
```

Michael Y: ok that explains it. For tiny-seq latency SLO we prefer lower startup overhead. Can we pin kernel selector fallback for the canary?
Kevin M: yes — we can set kernel_selector.prefer = legacy-fp16 for the canary pool. Quick change: `rbctl config set runtime.batcher.kernel_preference=legacy-fp16 --targets=canary`
Rachel B: KV reuse dropped slightly because larger min_batch_fill reduced opportunities for prefix reuse — small requests no longer aligned into the old microbatching windows. Hit ratio drop ~3pp.
Anya L: mitigation options: 1) revert batcher.min_batch_fill 2) pin kernel preference to legacy for canary 3) throttle canary traffic to 2% until we fix autotuner. Which to do now?
Kevin M: I'll do (1) to restore baseline and then follow with (2) while we iterate on smarter kernel heuristics. Doing rollback now.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated by Kevin M: rollback config runtime.batcher.min_batch_fill -> 0.05 at 1917654335
observability-bot: Canary rollback completed at 1917654350. p99 back to ~85ms within ~15s of rollback. KV hit ratio recovered to 0.73.
Anya L: :thumbsup: nice quick backout. We'll still need a follow-up — kernel-autoselect needs to consider per-sequence startup cost not just throughput.
Sasha P: Agreed. Filing a follow-up ticket with profiler traces and a reproducible load test. I'll include microbench scripts and a small-seq workload harness.
Michael Y: Next immediate step: add a guard to autotuner to avoid switching to high-setup-overhead kernels when small-seq fraction > 40%. I'll put a draft PR.
Rachel B: also adding an alert to detect p95->p99 divergence > 100ms for tiny-seq route so we don't rely on manual eyeballing.
Anya L: thanks all. Postmortem and follow-ups pinned to #eng-runtime during incident. :eyes:
